args.query: WEAK_SIGNAL camera offline RSSI -83 dBm fix repeater

results.text: Customer reported a CAM-S1 in a detached garage going offline several times a day. RSSI was -86 dBm; all other devices normal. Installing an RP-1 repeater solved it. Resolved at frontline.

Peripherals talk to the base station over a sub-GHz proprietary radio. Signal strength (RSSI) is shown in Device Settings > Device Info. Above -70 dBm is good, -70 to -80 dBm is acceptable, below -80 dBm causes intermittent disconnections, delayed notifications and choppy live view. Concrete walls, metal doors and fridges strongly attenuate the signal. Fix: move the device or base station, or install the official RP-1 repeater.

results.text: Three sensors in different rooms went offline at the same minute; base station online, RSSI history normal, E-610 in log. Restarting did not help. Escalated; radio module replaced. Escalated correctly.

results.text: CAM-S1 runs on a rechargeable battery lasting 3 to 6 months. Below 10 percent the camera disables live view and may miss events; below 3 percent it goes offline. Charge with the supplied USB-C cable for about 6 hours. Frequent motion events in busy areas shorten battery life; enable power-saving mode.

complaint: Our garage camera has been offline for two days. The garage is at the far end of the house, so I assume the signal is just too weak out there. Is there a booster or repeater I can buy? Everything else seems to work fine and I haven't changed anything in the app.
usability_reason: The response is clear and polite, and it accurately summarizes the symptom and the failed relocation test without overclaiming a fix. However, actionability is weak: the customer asked about buying a booster/repeater, and the reply only says engineering will investigate with no concrete next step, timeline, or answer about the repeater. It also does not clearly explain that the weak-signal theory was ruled out by the customer's test, leaving the customer without guidance.
